records.title: Seigal's Conjecture on Gram Determinants of Real Binary Tensors Fails for n ≥ 4
records.description:
For a real tensor of format 2×⋯×2 with n factors, let d_i be the determinant of the Gram matrix M_i M_i^T of its i-th flattening M_i. Seigal called the set of tuples (d_1, …, d_n) of tensors in the Frobenius unit ball the Gram locus, described it for n = 3, and conjectured that for n ≥ 4 it is cut out of the cube [0, 1/4]^n by a single polynomial inequality Q_1 ≥ Q_2 (Linear Algebra Appl. 2018, Conjecture 1.5; Oberwolfach Reports 2017). We point out that this conjecture is false for every n ≥ 4. For instance, (9/100, 9/100, 9/100, 6/25) satisfies Q_1 > 500 Q_2 but is not the Gram tuple of any real or complex tensor in the unit ball, and the counterexamples form a set with nonempty interior. This is a short corollary of known results: by theorems of Domanov, Stegeman and De Lathauwer (2017), and of Higuchi, Sudbery and Szulc (2003) for complex tensors, plus an elementary step from the unit sphere to the unit ball, the Gram locus is the set of d ∈ [0, 1/4]^n with Σ_{j≠i} √(1 − 4d_j) − √(1 − 4d_i) ≤ n − 2 for all i. From this we obtain the correct n-ary form of Seigal's theorem for n = 3, a union of two basic semialgebraic sets given by explicit integer polynomials, and we show that for no n ≥ 3 is the Gram locus the nonnegativity set of a single polynomial inside the cube (for n = 2 it is). We also correct a misprinted inequality in Seigal's theorem for n = 3. This is an unrefereed note.

Unrefereed preprint released for independent mathematical scrutiny. Publication on Zenodo does not constitute peer review. AI-assisted tools supported research, computation, proof development, and manuscript preparation. The author remains responsible for all claims and the final text.

records.title: No single polynomial inequality defines a real binary Gram locus
records.description:
For a real tensor with n binary factors, the Gram locus is the tuple of determinants of its one-mode Gram matrices as the tensor ranges over the closed Frobenius unit ball. For every n>=3, no single real polynomial nonnegativity condition in those determinant coordinates defines this locus inside the cube [0,1/4]^n, or inside its known convex hull. This gives a negative answer to Seigal's single-polynomial question for n>=4. The self-contained proof uses established marginal polygon inequalities, an explicit real three-factor realization, exact polynomial multiplicities and zero-determinant slices. A strictly positive rational four-factor tuple also passes the proposed polynomial condition but is unrealizable at any allowed norm.

The marginal criteria and real constructions of Higuchi-Sudbery-Szulc, Bravyi and Domanov-Stegeman-De Lathauwer are credited antecedents. Sinn's earlier general boundary/interior obstruction is also credited. Alper Ferudun's unrefereed October 2, 2026 preprint, DOI10.5281/zenodo.23111048, contains an overlapping stronger theorem, including an all-positive domain. Our original theorem-bearing proof is present in GitHub PR170, created September 30, 2026 at13:15:23UTC, and is unchanged. We describe these as contemporaneous separate disclosures. Commit timestamps are author-controlled; current public repository visibility was verified, but historical visibility was not independently archived. This October12 formal preprint is not backdated. records.title: Off-interval spectral convergence for geometrically consistent discrete dipoles
records.description: We give an independent proof of the off-interval eigenvalue approximation described in Costabel's OWR43/2022 discrete-dipole question, under an explicit geometric condition: center-selected cubic voxel unions converge in volume to the bounded measurable particle. This includes every bounded Lipschitz particle, for arbitrary grid translations. At every fixed complex frequency, the actual zero-diagonal matrices have no spectral pollution outside the exact static lattice interval, uniform resolvent stability there, and approximation of isolated eigenvalues with algebraic multiplicity, norm-convergent embedded Riesz projections and generalized spectral subspaces. The proof combines Costabel--Dauge--Nedaiasl's established static lattice interval with strong static consistency, Hilbert--Schmidt convergence of the actual sampled dynamic correction and classical compact spectral approximation. A separate compact positive-volume empty-interior support has a nonreal continuum pole at frequency1/10000 while every matrix on the rational meshes is 3x3 zero; its support index is existential. This does not refute convergence for regular particles or establish a necessary geometry condition. Cubic DDA consistency, general spectral principles, continuum pole theory and sphere perturbation are credited prior work. A named 2022/2023 time-harmonic DDA manuscript was not located in the bounded audit, Rahola's full article was unavailable, and a forward-citing thesis was screened only at metadata/abstract level. These priority limitations remain explicit; no first-priority, new general theory or unrestricted compact-support resolution is claimed. The deposit contains an analytical research note and a source/verification archive with original artifacts, exact symbolic/rational controls, illustrative numerical diagnostics and authored adversarial audits. Finite computations supplement rather than replace the proof and do not certify historical priority. AI tools were used extensively in development, derivation, computation, literature research, writing and independent internal adversarial checking. This is an unrefereed preprint without external human peer review or proof-assistant formalization.
